Knighton Close.road: Narrow cul-de-sac, no centre line, parking in a shared forecourt in front of the houses.
Knighton Close.note: A short terrace of 1960s/70s three-storey townhouses in buff brick with pale cladding on the upper floor and dormers in a brown tile roof; the other view is just a hedge and bank.

Badgers Rise.road: Narrow curving estate road on a hill, no centre line, no markings, footway on one side.
Badgers Rise.note: 1980s estate of small detached and semi houses and link garages in red and buff brick with brown concrete tile roofs, open lawns and drives, wooded hillside behind.

Newlands Avenue.road: Two-lane residential road without centre line, wide grass verges with trees, yellow lines near the junction.
Newlands Avenue.note: Interwar semis and bungalows in red brick, some with white-rendered upper floors and bay windows, behind low brick walls; a long stretch of tall fence and hedge on one side.

Sheepwalk.road: Narrow sloping road, no centre line, footway on one side.
Sheepwalk.note: Hillside 1960s/70s chalet bungalows and detached houses in red brick with brown tile roofs and box dormers, raised gardens behind red-brick retaining walls.

Marshland Square.road: Two-lane residential road, no centre line, grass verges between road and footway, on-street parking.
Marshland Square.note: Postwar hipped-roof semis with red brick ground floors and cream/white rendered upper floors, brown tile roofs, behind tall privet hedges; two of four views are just trees and shrubs.

Hemdean Hill.road: Narrow sloping residential street, no centre line, white edge/parking line, kerbside parking.
Hemdean Hill.note: Victorian red-brick terraces and semis with slate roofs, white-painted bay windows and tall chimneys, behind low brick walls; one side has a long old rendered garden wall and garages.

Briar Close.road: Hillside cul-de-sac with a grassed turning-circle island, no centre line or markings.
Briar Close.note: 1960s hillside close of red-brick detached houses with white-panelled or rendered gable fronts and red-brick bungalows, brown tile roofs, open lawns and steep drives, wooded hill behind.

Southdown Road.road: Two-lane residential road without centre line, grass verges, houses on raised banks reached by steps; one side is a wooded bank.
Southdown Road.note: Postwar hipped-roof semis with red-brick ground floors and cream-rendered upper floors, brown tile roofs, set up on grassy banks with hedges; one view is just woodland.

The Rise.road: Private-looking narrow access road with no markings, lamp posts on grass.
The Rise.note: A large white-rendered Regency/Victorian villa with a columned porch behind a clipped hedge, plus a red-brick garage block; heavily treed and only two views.

Sheldon Rise.road: Views are taken from Hemdean Road at the junction: wide two-lane road with dashed centre line, grass verges with young trees.
Sheldon Rise.note: From the Hemdean Road junction: 1980s/90s red-brick detached houses with brown tile roofs and open gravel drives; the views show the road corner more than the close itself.

School Lane.road: Narrow residential lane, no centre line, side roads with give-way lines, off-street parking bays in front of the flats.
School Lane.note: A mix: four-storey 1960s red-brick council flats with blue window panels set in lawns, 1980s/90s red-brick houses and a small hipped-roof flats block, and postwar semis behind picket fences further along.

The Cloisters.road: Both views are from Priest Hill at the entrance: two-lane road with dashed centre line, bus stop box and give-way markings.
The Cloisters.note: The views only show the entrance off Priest Hill, screened by tall conifers and hedges; the only buildings visible are distant red-brick Edwardian houses on Priest Hill, so the close itself is unseen.

Fallowfield Close.road: Quiet narrow cul-de-sac, no markings, footway on one side.
Fallowfield Close.note: 1960s/70s red-brick detached houses with white Georgian-style windows and a full-width porch roof, plus a bungalow, behind lawns and tall hedges; one view is mostly fence.

The Gardeners.road: New estate road joining Surley Row (which has a centre line and SLOW marking); give-way line at the mouth, block-paved footway.
The Gardeners.note: A recent (2010s) development of red-brick detached and semi houses with orange-red tile roofs and white gable boards, set behind post-and-rail fences off Surley Row.

Greycoat Court.note: Both links open an indoor photosphere inside Queen Anne's School (a drama studio), not the street; no usable street imagery.

Springfield Mews.road: Narrow private mews drive, no markings, block-paved and gravel surfaces.
Springfield Mews.note: 1990s/2000s detached houses with red-brick ground floors and white-rendered gables with arched windows and dark tile roofs, behind low brick walls with railings; down a side drive is an older white-rendered villa.

Buckingham Gate.road: Small private cul-de-sac with no markings, block-paved drives.
Buckingham Gate.note: 1980s/90s red-brick detached houses with attached garages and brown tile roofs among dense hedges and trees; one of two views is just hedge.

Victoria Road.road: Views from the Hemdean Road junction: give-way lines into Hemdean Road, which has a centre line, double yellow lines and a school KEEP CLEAR zigzag.
Victoria Road.note: Edwardian semis with red-brick ground floors and white-rendered upper floors, some with black-and-white timbered gables and tile roofs, behind low brick walls and hedges; the other view shows a school building on Hemdean Road.

St Lukes Way.road: Short access road with a marked car park; no centre line.
St Lukes Way.note: A long two-storey 1990s red-brick care home with a hipped dark tile roof set in lawns and a car park, and a red-brick flats block behind tall clipped conifer hedges.

Grove Hill Close.road: Block-paved private close with parking, no markings.
Grove Hill Close.note: Only one usable view: a modern white-rendered building with grey timber cladding above a castellated block retaining wall, around a block-paved parking court; the other view is just hedge and trees. Roof not visible.

Buckside.road: Both views are at the junction with Church Road (A4074): busy two-lane road with centre line, double yellow lines, give-way markings, zigzags and a SLOW marking.
Buckside.shops: Facing Church Road: a short parade with a black-and-white mock-Tudor gabled cafe/restaurant with a striped awning and outdoor seating, then two-storey shops with dark fascias and residential gables above; roughly half the visible frontage is shops.
Buckside.note: Views are from Church Road at the corner of Buckside: Edwardian red-brick and white-rendered buildings with gables, a mock-Tudor corner cafe and a long red-brick boundary wall; a later red-brick house with dormers on the corner.

Surley Place.road: Views are at Scott Close junction: sloping two-lane road with dashed centre line, give-way markings, red-brick retaining walls and a garage court.
Surley Place.note: Only distant views: red-brick 1980s/90s houses with dark tile roofs and white-boarded gables beyond the junction, retaining walls and a garage block; the place itself is barely visible.

Hare Warren Court.road: Block-paved private courtyard with parking, brick gate piers, no markings.
Hare Warren Court.note: 1990s/2000s three-storey red-brick flats with cream-rendered top floors, small balconies and dormers, around a block-paved car court, plus a red-brick gabled house and a timber bin store.

Burcombe Way.road: Narrow estate road, no markings, parking along the kerb, garage block on a corner.
Burcombe Way.note: 1960s/70s two-storey red-brick terraces with shallow-pitched roofs and white panels under the windows, seen behind rear fences, sheds and a red-brick garage; little of the frontages is visible.

St Peter's Hill.road: Views are from the A4074 at the entrance: wide main road, entrance between brick gate piers with a gravel drive.
St Peter's Hill.note: From the main road entrance: modern detached houses with red-brick ground floors and cream-rendered upper floors behind brick gate piers, mostly hidden by dense hedges and trees.

Westonbirt Drive.road: Views are at the Graveney Drive junction: narrow road without centre line, one footway, wooded bank opposite.
Westonbirt Drive.note: Only one house visible: a 1970s dark-red/brown brick detached house with a dark tile roof and solar panels, set among woodland; the other view is solid vegetation.

Lymington Gate.road: Views from Kelvedon Way: wide quiet estate road, no centre line, footways both sides, dropped kerbs to drives.
Lymington Gate.note: 1960s red-brick bungalows with brown concrete tile roofs and white uPVC windows behind low red-brick walls, with a few two-storey houses and pitched-roof garages.

Mardy.note: 1990s/2000s red-brick detached houses with dark tile roofs, small canopy porches and integral garages, behind small lawns and shrubs; the other view (2012 imagery) is a conifer hedge.

Scolars Close.road: Views are from St Peter's Hill: two-lane road with no centre line here, wide grass verge on one side, mature trees both sides.
Scolars Close.note: Both views are from St Peter's Hill and show mostly mature trees, close-board fences and hedges; only a couple of distant red-brick houses are visible.

High Meadow.road: Narrow residential road, no markings, footway on one side.
High Meadow.note: Bungalows and chalet bungalows with white-rendered walls and brown tile roofs, seen over tall close-board fences and hedges; few frontages visible.

Auburn Court.road: Views from Church Road (A4074): two-lane road with double yellow lines, give-way markings and a bollarded footway into an old lane.
Auburn Court.note: From Church Road: a three-storey 1960s red-brick flats block with white-boarded window bands and hipped roof, plus an old red-brick and flint cottage group with orange clay tile roofs behind flint walls.

Atterbury Gardens.road: Views from Woodford Close: narrow estate road, no markings, open-plan drives.
Atterbury Gardens.note: From the Woodford Close end: 1980s red-brick and buff-brick detached houses with brown tile roofs and open drives; the gated entrance and brick piers to Atterbury Gardens itself are hidden by trees.

Conisboro Way.road: Wide estate road (2012 imagery) with grass verges, no centre line, concrete-slab carriageway.
Conisboro Way.note: 2012 imagery: postwar red-brick semis/short terraces with brown tile roofs and open lawns behind wide grass verges; the other view is a blurred site cabin on a corner plot.

Bramblings.road: Quiet estate cul-de-sac, no markings, open-plan lawns to the kerb.
Bramblings.note: 1980s houses in orange-red brick with tile-hung upper floors (and some black weatherboarding), steep dark-brown tile roofs with dormers and catslide garages, open-plan front lawns.

Hornbeam Close.road: Views from Kidmore Road: two-lane road without centre line here, grass verge with big street trees, give-way at junctions.
Hornbeam Close.note: From Kidmore Road at the entrance: interwar red-brick semis with gable fronts and white-rendered gable panels behind hedges and low walls, under big street trees; a small parade of shops is visible further along Kidmore Road.

Blossom Road.road: Narrow modern estate road with block-paved parking courts, no markings.
Blossom Road.note: 2000s three-storey red-brick flats with roof dormers and rooflights, white uPVC windows and dark tile roofs, beside parking courts, with red-brick houses beyond.

Valley Close.road: Small cul-de-sac with a grassed turning circle, no markings.
Valley Close.note: 1930s-style semis in red brick with white-rendered two-storey bay windows and gables, arched porches and hipped dark tile roofs, behind low brick walls with paved and lawned drives.

Boundary Lane.road: Narrow wooded lane near The Warren, no markings, gravel verges.
Boundary Lane.note: A Victorian Gothic red-brick lodge with steep gables, stone-mullioned windows and dark tile roofs behind brick gate piers and railings on a low wall; the other view is dense trees.

Woodrow Court.road: Private car park/access drive with shrub beds, no markings.
Woodrow Court.note: Mostly shrubs, a wooded bank and a car park; only the corner of a red-brick, tile-hung 1980s-looking flats block is visible.

Chelford Way.road: Quiet residential road, no centre line, footway one side, gravel drives.
Chelford Way.note: 1960s/70s red-brick detached houses with white-framed windows, side carports and brown tile roofs behind lawns and shrubs; the other view is a building-site hoarding in front of a tile-hung chalet house under scaffolding.

Lawson Drive.road: Views are from Conisboro Avenue: wide two-lane road with dashed centre line, footways both sides, grass verge on one side.
Lawson Drive.note: From Conisboro Avenue at the junction: 1930s red-brick semis with white-rendered bays and gables and hipped dark tile roofs behind hedges and low brick walls; Lawson Drive itself is not directly seen.

Woodberry Close.road: Small cul-de-sac with grass verges and a turning head, no markings.
Woodberry Close.note: 1930s-style semis in red brick with white-rendered two-storey bays and gables, arched porches and hipped brown tile roofs, behind low brick walls and paved drives - same builder as Valley Close.

Regency Heights.road: Views are from Woodford Close: quiet estate road, no centre line, give-way line at the junction, block-paved drives.
Regency Heights.note: From the Woodford Close end: 1960s/70s link-detached houses in red/buff brick with dark-stained timber and white-boarded upper panels and balconies, low-pitched tile roofs, open-plan fronts; a short drive leads to newer red-brick gabled houses (Regency Heights proper) in the distance.
